rules.explanation: This setting specifies the path and file name used for Windows Defender Firewall Public profile logging.
rules.impact: Without a defined log path, Public profile firewall events may not be available for review. Logging supports detection and investigation of suspicious activity on untrusted networks.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile log file size
rules.explanation: This setting configures the maximum size of the Windows Defender Firewall Public profile log file. A common baseline minimum is 16,384 KB.
rules.impact: An undersized log rolls over quickly and may omit evidence needed during incident response. Adequate log size improves retention of Public profile firewall events.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile log dropped packets
rules.explanation: This setting enables logging of dropped packets (DROP events) for Windows Defender Firewall in the Public profile.
rules.impact: Dropped-packet records help reconstruct blocked connection attempts during investigations. Without them, analysis of denied traffic on public networks is incomplete.

rules.title: Windows Firewall Public profile log successful connections
rules.explanation: This setting enables logging of successful connections (ALLOW events) for Windows Defender Firewall in the Public profile.
rules.impact: Successful-connection records provide context for permitted traffic during investigations. Including ALLOW events improves completeness of Public profile firewall telemetry.

rules.title: Credential Validation auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records the results of credential validation for a user account logon request. Events are generated on the computer that validates the credentials: a domain controller for domain accounts, or the local computer for local accounts.
rules.impact: Credential validation events help investigators identify failed and successful authentication attempts and support detection of password guessing and unauthorized logon activity.

rules.title: Application Group Management auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records changes to application groups used by Windows Authorization Manager for role-based access control (RBAC) in applications.
rules.impact: Application group management events help detect unauthorized changes to application roles and support investigation of privilege-related incidents.

rules.title: Computer Account Management auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records creation, modification, and deletion of computer accounts in Active Directory or on the local system.
rules.impact: Computer account management events help detect unauthorized machine account changes that may indicate privilege escalation or domain compromise.

rules.title: Other Account Management Events auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records account management activity that is not covered by more specific account management subcategories.
rules.impact: Other account management events provide additional evidence for detecting and investigating unauthorized privilege changes.
rules.parser: $.Auditpol.[?(@.Policy=='Other Account Management Events' || @.Policy=='Другие события управления учетной записью' )].Setting

rules.title: Security Group Management auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records security group management activity, including creation, modification, or deletion of groups and addition or removal of members.
rules.impact: Security group changes often grant or remove privileged access. Auditing these events supports detection of malicious or accidental privilege escalation.

rules.title: User Account Management auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records user account management events such as creating, modifying, deleting, renaming, enabling, or disabling accounts, and setting or changing passwords.
rules.impact: User account management events help identify unauthorized account creation or modification and support investigation of credential and privilege abuse.

rules.title: Plug and Play Events auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records Plug and Play activity, including connection of external devices detected by the system.
rules.impact: Plug and Play audit events help IT staff identify unauthorized device attachments that may be used for data exfiltration or malware introduction.

rules.title: Process Creation auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records process creation events and identifies the program and user context that started the process.
rules.impact: Process creation events provide critical evidence for malware execution analysis, lateral movement tracing, and broader security incident investigation.

rules.title: Account Lockout auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records instances when a user account is locked out after multiple failed logon attempts.
rules.impact: Account lockout events help detect password-guessing attacks and support investigation of authentication-related security incidents.

rules.title: Group Membership auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records group membership information present in a user's logon token. Events are generated on the computer where the logon session is created (interactive or network).
rules.impact: Group membership audit events clarify which privileges were effective at logon and help investigate unauthorized use of elevated group memberships.

rules.title: Logoff auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records when a user logs off a computer. Events are generated on the accessed system: the interactive workstation for interactive sessions, or the resource host for network logons.
rules.impact: Logoff events complete the session timeline needed to determine who accessed systems and when those sessions ended during incident investigation.

rules.title: Logon auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records user logon attempts on the computer that was accessed. Interactive logons are logged on the local workstation; network logons to shared resources are logged on the resource host.
rules.impact: Without logon auditing, it is difficult or impossible to determine which accounts accessed or attempted to access organizational computers.

rules.title: Other Logon/Logoff Events auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records additional logon and logoff activity, including Remote Desktop Services disconnect and reconnect, RunAs process starts under another account, and workstation lock and unlock.
rules.impact: These events provide visibility into privileged session activity and console state changes that are important during security incident investigation.
rules.parser: $.Auditpol.[?(@.Policy=='Other Logon/Logoff Events' || @.Policy=='Другие события входа и выхода' )].Setting

rules.title: Special Logon auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records special logon events. A special logon assigns elevated privileges comparable to administrative rights and can be used to elevate a process.
rules.impact: Special logon events help detect privileged session use and support investigation of unauthorized elevation of rights.

rules.title: Removable Storage auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records user attempts to access file system objects on removable storage devices. Success and failure audits can be generated for requested access types when the policy is enabled.
rules.impact: Removable storage auditing helps detect and investigate potential data exfiltration, such as copying sensitive files to USB media.

rules.title: Audit Policy Change auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records changes to audit policy, including modifications that affect System Access Control Lists (SACLs).
rules.impact: Audit policy change events help detect attempts to disable or weaken auditing and preserve evidence needed for security incident investigation.

rules.title: Authentication Policy Change auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records changes to authentication policy settings that govern how credentials are validated.
rules.impact: Unauthorized authentication policy changes can weaken logon controls. Auditing these events supports detection and investigation of such modifications.

rules.title: Authorization Policy Change auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records changes to authorization policy settings that control access decisions.
rules.impact: Unauthorized authorization policy changes can expand privileges or weaken access controls. Auditing these events supports detection and investigation.

rules.title: Sensitive Privilege Use auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records when a user or service account exercises sensitive privileges that can affect protected system resources or confidential data.
rules.impact: Sensitive privilege use events help identify misuse of powerful rights and provide evidence for security incident investigation.
rules.parser: $.Auditpol.[?(@.Policy=='Sensitive Privilege Use' || @.Policy=='Использование прав, затрагивающее конфиденциальные данные' )].Setting

rules.title: IPsec Driver auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records Internet Protocol security (IPsec) driver activity related to secured network communications.
rules.impact: IPsec driver events help diagnose failures in protected communications and support investigation of attacks against IPsec-enforced traffic.

rules.title: Other System Events auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records miscellaneous system security events that are not covered by more specific system audit categories.
rules.impact: Other system events can indicate Windows Firewall failures and related system security issues that require investigation.

rules.title: Security State Change auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records changes to the security state of the system, such as starting and stopping the security subsystem.
rules.impact: Security state change events help detect unexpected restarts or shutdowns of security components during incident investigation.

rules.title: Security System Extension auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records loading of extension code by the security subsystem, such as authentication packages.
rules.impact: Security system extension events help detect unauthorized authentication packages or other security subsystem extensions that may indicate compromise.

rules.title: System Integrity auditing enabled
rules.explanation: This audit subcategory records integrity violations affecting the security subsystem.
rules.impact: System integrity events help detect attempts to undermine the security subsystem and provide evidence for security incident investigation.

rules.title: Lock screen camera disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the camera can be used while the lock screen is displayed.
rules.impact: A camera available on the lock screen may allow unauthorized image or video capture without an authenticated session.

rules.title: Lock screen slideshow disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether a slideshow of images can run on the lock screen.
rules.impact: Slideshow content may expose sensitive images left in the slideshow folder to anyone with physical access to the console before sign-in.

rules.title: Disable input personalization
rules.explanation: This policy controls whether input personalization and automatic learning features may collect typing and speech input data. When disabled, automatic learning for input personalization is turned off.
rules.impact: Input personalization can capture sensitive keystrokes or phrases and contribute to telemetry sent to Microsoft. Disabling it reduces collection and outbound sharing of potentially confidential input data.

rules.title: Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) enabled
rules.explanation: This check verifies that the Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) Group Policy client-side extension is present so managed local administrator accounts receive unique, centrally recoverable passwords.
rules.impact: Without LAPS, local administrator passwords are often shared or rarely rotated across domain-joined workstations, increasing lateral-movement risk after a single credential compromise.

rules.title: LAPS password expiration protection enabled
rules.explanation: When Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) is used, this policy enforces Password Settings Object (PSO) age limits so the managed local administrator password cannot be reset to a longer lifetime. This requirement applies only to servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: LAPS provides unique, periodically rotated passwords for local administrator accounts on domain-joined systems. Without expiration protection, password age can be extended, increasing the window for credential reuse and compromise.

rules.title: LAPS local administrator password management enabled
rules.explanation: This setting enables LAPS management of the local administrator password on domain-joined systems. This requirement applies only to servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Without LAPS, local administrator passwords are often shared or rarely rotated, increasing the risk that a single compromised credential can be reused across many systems.

rules.title: LAPS password complexity configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the password complexity requirements applied by LAPS to the managed local administrator account. This requirement applies only to servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Weak local administrator passwords increase the likelihood of brute-force or password-guessing attacks against privileged local accounts.

rules.title: Configure LAPS password length
rules.explanation: This Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) policy sets the required length of managed local administrator passwords. It applies to domain-joined member servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Short or weak local administrator passwords increase the risk of privilege escalation and lateral movement. Adequate LAPS password length strengthens unique local admin credentials across managed hosts.

rules.title: LAPS password age configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the maximum age, in days, of the LAPS-managed local administrator password before it is rotated. This requirement applies only to servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Infrequent password rotation lengthens the useful life of a stolen local administrator credential and increases lateral-movement risk.

rules.title: Automatic administrator logon disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows automatically signs in with a stored administrator account at startup (AutoAdminLogon).
rules.impact: Automatic logon grants console access without credentials and stores the account password in the registry in clear text, exposing the system to anyone with physical or local registry access.

rules.title: Configure IPv6 source routing protection level
rules.explanation: This TCP/IPv6 parameter controls how the system handles IPv6 source-routed packets. DisableIPSourceRouting determines whether source routing is permitted, restricted, or fully disabled.
rules.impact: IP source routing can be abused for spoofing and traffic-redirection attacks that bypass expected network paths. Restricting or disabling it reduces susceptibility to those network-layer techniques.

rules.title: IPv4 source routing protection level configured
rules.explanation: This setting configures how the system handles IPv4 packets that use IP source routing.
rules.impact: Permissive source routing can assist IP spoofing and traffic-redirection attacks by allowing packets to specify their own path through the network.

rules.title: Dial-Up Networking saved password feature disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables the ability to save passwords for remote access connections that use Dial-Up Networking (RasMan DisableSavePassword).
rules.impact: Saved remote-access credentials on a lost or stolen device can give an attacker immediate access to the corporate network without needing to obtain the password interactively.

rules.title: ICMP redirects disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the system accepts ICMP redirect messages that can alter existing IP routes.
rules.impact: Accepting ICMP redirects allows an attacker to manipulate routing so traffic is diverted to an unintended host, enabling interception or follow-on attacks.

rules.title: TCP keep-alive time configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines how often TCP keep-alive packets are sent to verify that an idle connection is still valid.
rules.impact: An unbounded or poorly chosen keep-alive interval can be abused to maintain or amplify connection load and contribute to denial-of-service conditions.

rules.title: NetBIOS name-release requests ignored except from WINS
rules.explanation: This setting configures NetBIOS over TCP/IP to ignore name-release requests that do not originate from WINS servers (NoNameReleaseOnDemand).
rules.impact: Honoring unsolicited NetBIOS name-release requests can allow an attacker to force name conflicts, enabling NetBIOS name spoofing and denial-of-service against name resolution.

rules.title: IRDP router discovery disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the system performs ICMP Router Discovery Protocol (IRDP) to locate routers on the local network.
rules.impact: With IRDP enabled, a compromised host on the subnet can advertise itself as a router and cause other systems to forward traffic through it.

rules.title: Safe DLL search mode enabled
rules.explanation: Safe DLL Search Mode changes the order in which Windows searches for DLLs so that system directories are preferred over the current working directory.
rules.impact: Without Safe DLL Search Mode, applications may load a malicious DLL placed in a writable directory ahead of the legitimate system library, enabling code execution.

rules.title: Screen saver grace period configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the delay, in seconds, between screen saver activation and the workstation becoming locked.
rules.impact: An excessive grace period leaves an unlocked interactive session available after the screen saver starts, increasing the risk of unauthorized console access.

rules.title: TCP max data retransmissions (IPv6) configured
rules.explanation: This setting limits the number of TCP data segment retransmissions used when establishing or maintaining TCP connections over IPv6 (TcpMaxDataRetransmissions).
rules.impact: An unbounded retransmission count can be abused to prolong connection attempts and contribute to denial-of-service conditions against network services.

rules.title: TCP maximum data retransmissions configured
rules.explanation: This setting limits how many times unacknowledged TCP data segments are retransmitted before the connection is abandoned.
rules.impact: Unlimited or excessive retransmissions can be leveraged to prolong resource consumption and contribute to denial-of-service against TCP services.

rules.title: Security event log warning level configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the percentage of Security event log capacity at which a warning is generated that the log is approaching capacity.
rules.impact: Without timely capacity warnings, the Security log may fill and stop recording new events, reducing visibility for incident detection and investigation.

rules.title: NetBIOS node type set to P-node (WINS only)
rules.explanation: This setting configures the NetBIOS over TCP/IP node type so name resolution uses point-to-point queries to WINS (P-node) rather than broadcast-based methods.
rules.impact: Broadcast name resolution exposes NetBIOS name queries on the local network, which attackers can observe or spoof. P-node reduces that broadcast traffic and related attack opportunities.

rules.title: LLMNR multicast name resolution disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution (LLMNR), which resolves names on the local subnet using multicast queries.
rules.impact: LLMNR can be abused with malicious multicast responses to redirect name resolution and facilitate credential capture or man-in-the-middle attacks.

rules.title: Third-party font providers disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows can download and use fonts from third-party font providers.
rules.impact: Third-party font providers introduce unapproved content and network calls that expand the attack surface and can conflict with enterprise change-control requirements.

rules.title: Insecure guest logons to SMB shares disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the SMB client may use insecure guest authentication when connecting to file shares.
rules.impact: Insecure guest logons allow unauthenticated access to shared resources and can expose sensitive data without accountability.

rules.title: LLTDIO mapper I/O disabled on domain networks
rules.explanation: This setting controls the Link-Layer Topology Discovery Mapper I/O (LLTDIO) driver on domain-joined networks used for network map discovery.
rules.impact: Network topology discovery can expose the host to unauthorized or attacker-controlled devices that participate in topology mapping.

rules.title: LLTD Responder (RSPNDR) disabled on domain networks
rules.explanation: This setting controls the Link-Layer Topology Discovery Responder (RSPNDR) driver on domain-joined networks.
rules.impact: Responding to topology discovery requests can expose the host to unauthorized devices and assist mapping of the internal network.

rules.title: Peer-to-peer networking disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables Microsoft Peer-to-Peer Networking (Peernet) on the system.
rules.impact: Peer-to-peer networking creates ad hoc connectivity paths that are difficult to control and can be abused for unauthorized data transfer or lateral communication.

rules.title: Network bridge creation disabled on domain networks
rules.explanation: This setting prevents users from creating or modifying a network bridge when Network Location Awareness identifies a domain network.
rules.impact: A network bridge can join otherwise separate networks and allow unintended traffic flow between them, which an attacker can abuse for pivoting or data exfiltration.

rules.title: Internet Connection Sharing UI disabled
rules.explanation: This setting removes the user interface for enabling Internet Connection Sharing (ICS) as an Internet gateway.
rules.impact: ICS can turn a workstation into an uncontrolled Internet gateway, bypassing perimeter controls and allowing unmanaged outbound access.

rules.title: Standard domain users prohibited from setting network location
rules.explanation: This setting requires elevation when a standard domain user attempts to change the network location (for example, when mapping or classifying a network connection).
rules.impact: Allowing standard users to set network location increases the attack surface by permitting changes that can weaken firewall profiles or network trust boundaries.

rules.title: IPv6 disabled
rules.explanation: Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) is the successor to IPv4 for addressing and routing on local networks and the Internet. This setting disables IPv6 components through the Tcpip6 DisabledComponents value.
rules.impact: Where IPv6 is unused, leaving it enabled expands the network attack surface and can complicate traffic monitoring. Disabling IPv6 reduces unused protocol exposure on managed endpoints.

rules.title: Windows Connect Now registrars disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables Windows Connect Now (WCN) registrar functionality used for simplified wireless configuration and credential transfer.
rules.impact: WCN simplifies wireless provisioning and can be abused to propagate network credentials or configurations to unauthorized devices.

rules.title: Disable Windows Connect Now wizard
rules.explanation: This policy disables the Windows Connect Now (WCN) user interface wizard used for simplified wireless network setup. WCN UI-assisted configuration transfer features are unavailable when disabled.
rules.impact: WCN simplifies distribution of wireless configurations and can be misused to deploy or obtain network settings during an attack. Disabling the wizard reduces that wireless configuration abuse path.

rules.title: Simultaneous Internet or domain connections minimized
rules.explanation: This Windows Connection Manager policy limits how computers establish multiple simultaneous connections to the Internet or a Windows domain.
rules.impact: Multiple concurrent connections can create uncontrolled paths to external networks and complicate enforcement of corporate connectivity policy.

rules.title: Simultaneous domain and non-domain connections blocked
rules.explanation: This setting determines whether a system may connect to a domain network and a non-domain network at the same time.
rules.impact: Concurrent domain and public network connections increase the risk that corporate traffic is exposed or routed through less trusted networks.

rules.title: Automatic connection to open Wi-Fi hotspots disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows may automatically connect to open wireless hotspots offered through OEM Wi-Fi network manager configuration (AutoConnectAllowedOEM).
rules.impact: Automatic association with open hotspots can place workstations on untrusted networks and expose them to traffic interception, captive-portal abuse, or other network-based attacks.

rules.title: UAC token filtering for remote local accounts enabled
rules.explanation: LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy controls whether remote network logons using local accounts receive a full elevated token or a filtered UAC token.
rules.impact: Local account credentials are frequently targeted. Applying UAC filtering to remote local-account logons reduces the privileges available to an attacker using stolen local credentials over the network.

rules.title: WDigest credential caching disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether WDigest authentication stores a reusable copy of the user's clear-text password in memory (UseLogonCredential).
rules.impact: When WDigest caching is enabled, clear-text credentials in LSASS memory can be recovered by an attacker with local privileged access.

rules.title: Process creation command-line auditing excluded
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether command-line arguments are included in process creation audit events.
rules.impact: Including command-line details in audit events can expose secrets such as passwords or tokens to anyone who can read the Security log.

rules.title: Early Launch Anti-Malware driver load policy configured
rules.explanation: This Early Launch Anti-Malware (ELAM) policy defines which boot-start drivers are allowed to initialize based on the ELAM driver's classification.
rules.impact: Without a restrictive driver load policy, untrusted boot-start drivers may load before antimalware protection is active and execute malicious code at boot.

rules.title: Background Group Policy processing enabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Group Policy is refreshed in the background without requiring a reboot or user re-logon.
rules.impact: Without background refresh, systems may continue operating under outdated security settings until the next restart or interactive logon.

rules.title: Group Policy processing forced even when GPOs are unchanged
rules.explanation: This setting forces Group Policy to reapply domain policy even when the GPO list has not changed since the last refresh.
rules.impact: Forcing policy reapplication helps restore intended domain security settings after unauthorized local changes.

rules.title: Cross-device experience (CDP) disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the device may participate in cross-device experiences that share activity and connectivity with other user devices (Continue experiences / CDP).
rules.impact: Cross-device communication expands trust relationships beyond the managed host and introduces additional paths for data exposure or abuse.

rules.title: Microsoft Store Open with access restricted
rules.explanation: This setting restricts use of Microsoft Store as an Open with target when searching for or launching applications from Explorer (NoUseStoreOpenWith).
rules.impact: Unrestricted Store Open with access can lead users to install or launch software outside enterprise-approved distribution channels.

rules.title: HTTP-based print driver downloads disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether print drivers can be downloaded over HTTP (Web PnP download).
rules.impact: Downloading drivers over HTTP lacks transport integrity guarantees and may allow users to obtain tampered drivers that contain malicious code.

rules.title: Disable handwriting personalization data sharing
rules.explanation: This Tablet PC policy prevents sharing of handwriting recognition personalization data. Handwriting samples collected for recognition improvement are not uploaded when data sharing is disabled.
rules.impact: Handwriting, including signatures, is personally identifiable information that many organizations must not transmit automatically. Disabling sharing reduces unauthorized disclosure of biometric-like personal data.

rules.title: Handwriting recognition error reports disabled
rules.explanation: This setting prevents the handwriting recognition error reporting tool from sending handwriting samples or related reports.
rules.impact: Handwriting samples can constitute personally identifiable information, including signatures, and automatic upload may violate privacy or data-handling policy.

rules.title: Internet Connection Wizard Microsoft ISP download disabled
rules.explanation: This setting configures the Internet Connection Wizard to exit rather than contact Microsoft to download an ISP list (ExitOnMSICW).
rules.impact: Unneeded outbound connections to retrieve ISP listings increase exposure and are typically unnecessary in managed enterprise environments.

rules.title: Disable Internet downloads for publishing and ordering wizards
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows publishing and Internet ordering wizards may download an updated list of online service providers.
rules.impact: Allowing these wizards to retrieve provider lists from the Internet introduces a limited risk of retrieving or loading untrusted content.

rules.title: Disable HTTP printing
rules.explanation: This setting determines whether documents may be sent to printers using the HTTP protocol.
rules.impact: HTTP printing transmits data without encryption, which increases the risk of interception or tampering on the network.

rules.title: Online Windows Registration Wizard disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables the Windows Registration Wizard so users cannot complete online product registration interactively.
rules.impact: In enterprise environments, individual online registration of Windows copies can create uncontrolled outbound connections and inconsistent asset registration.

rules.title: Search Companion content file updates disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables automatic download of content file updates used by Search Companion for local and Internet search.
rules.impact: Automatic content updates introduce an unnecessary external data path that can leak usage context from the managed environment.

rules.title: Online photo printing wizard disabled
rules.explanation: This setting removes online print-ordering tasks from the image Tasks pane so photos are not sent through the Online Print Ordering Wizard.
rules.impact: Online print ordering can transmit images and metadata to external services, creating a risk of unintended disclosure of sensitive content.

rules.title: Web publishing wizard tasks disabled
rules.explanation: This setting removes Explorer tasks such as "Publish this file to the Web", "Publish this folder to the Web", and "Publish the selected items to the Web".
rules.impact: Web publishing wizards provide a convenient path to upload files to external sites and can result in unintended disclosure of business data.

rules.title: Windows Messenger Customer Experience Improvement Program disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls participation in the Windows Messenger Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP).
rules.impact: CEIP can transmit software usage details to Microsoft, which is typically restricted in enterprise environments that limit third-party telemetry.

rules.title: Windows Customer Experience Improvement Program disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the Windows Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP) is enabled on the system.
rules.impact: CEIP can transmit software usage and diagnostic details to Microsoft, which is typically restricted where third-party telemetry is not approved.

rules.title: Disable Windows Error Reporting
rules.explanation: This setting disables Windows Error Reporting so that error and crash reports are not automatically submitted to Microsoft.
rules.impact: Error reports may include process, module, or user-context details that are sensitive in an enterprise environment.

rules.title: Kerberos device certificate authentication configured
rules.explanation: This setting configures Kerberos public key initiation (PKINIT) behavior for device authentication using a domain device certificate (DevicePKInitBehavior).
rules.impact: Certificate-based device authentication strengthens identity assurance beyond username and password alone and helps resist credential-only attacks against domain join identity.

rules.title: User input methods not copied to system logon account
rules.explanation: This setting prevents user-configured input methods (IMEs and keyboards) from being copied automatically to the system account for use on the sign-in screen.
rules.impact: Restricting custom input methods on the logon screen reduces exposure of the pre-authentication UI to user-installed input components.

rules.title: Prevent display of account details on the sign-in screen
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether users can show account details such as email address or user name on the Windows sign-in screen.
rules.impact: Account identifiers visible at the console or over Remote Desktop Services can help an attacker target password guessing, dictionary, or brute-force attacks against the last interactive user.

rules.title: Hide network selection UI on the sign-in screen
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the network selection user interface is available before a user signs in.
rules.impact: If network controls are available before authentication, an unauthorized person at the console can disconnect the system from the corporate network or join untrusted networks.

rules.title: Disable enumeration of connected users
rules.explanation: This setting restricts enumeration of currently connected (logged-on) users on domain-joined computers.
rules.impact: Enumerated account information can aid reconnaissance and subsequent credential-based attacks.

rules.title: Disable enumeration of local users on domain-joined computers
rules.explanation: This setting restricts enumeration of local user accounts on domain-joined computers at sign-in.
rules.impact: Local account names disclosed at the logon interface can support reconnaissance and targeted authentication attacks.

rules.title: Disable application notifications on the lock screen
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether applications may display notifications on the lock screen while the system is locked.
rules.impact: Lock-screen notifications can reveal sensitive organizational information to anyone who can view the console.

rules.title: Disable PIN sign-in for domain users
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether domain users may sign in with a convenience PIN under this policy.
rules.impact: PINs are often shorter and drawn from a smaller character space than domain passwords, which can reduce authentication strength for interactive access.

rules.title: Disable network connectivity during standby on battery
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the system maintains network connectivity while in standby when running on battery power.
rules.impact: Network availability during standby can leave an unattended system reachable to attackers even when the user believes the device is powered down.

rules.title: Disable network connectivity during standby when plugged in
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the system maintains network connectivity while in standby when connected to AC power.
rules.impact: Network availability during standby can leave an unattended system reachable to attackers even when the user believes the device is powered down.

rules.title: Require password on wake from sleep on battery
rules.explanation: This setting requires user credentials when the computer resumes from sleep while on battery power.
rules.impact: Without a wake password, anyone with physical access can resume an unattended system and continue an unlocked session.

rules.title: Require password on wake from sleep when plugged in
rules.explanation: This setting requires user credentials when the computer resumes from sleep while connected to AC power.
rules.impact: Without a wake password, anyone with physical access can resume an unattended system and continue an unlocked session.

rules.title: Disable unsolicited Remote Assistance
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether helpers may offer unsolicited Remote Assistance connections to the computer.
rules.impact: Unsolicited Remote Assistance can allow remote parties to connect to interactive sessions and potentially control the system or access sensitive data.

rules.title: Digitally sign secure channel data when possible
rules.explanation: This setting configures domain members to digitally sign secure channel traffic with a domain controller whenever signing can be negotiated. Logon data on the secure channel remains encrypted independently of full-channel encryption negotiation.
rules.impact: Without signing, secure channel traffic is authenticated and may encrypt sensitive items such as passwords, but lacks integrity protection for all traffic. Signing when possible strengthens channel integrity while still allowing negotiation with capable domain controllers.

rules.title: Enable RPC endpoint mapper client authentication
rules.explanation: This setting requires client authentication for RPC Endpoint Mapper resolution. It applies to servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Anonymous RPC Endpoint Mapper access can facilitate reconnaissance and attacks against RPC-exposed services.

rules.title: Restrict unauthenticated remote RPC clients
rules.explanation: This setting restricts remote RPC clients that do not authenticate, limiting anonymous access to RPC services. It applies to servers that are not domain controllers.
rules.impact: Unauthenticated remote RPC access can be leveraged for service enumeration and related attacks against the host.

rules.title: Disable MSDT remote support provider queries
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the Microsoft Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) may query remote support provider servers.
rules.impact: Diagnostic interactions with external support providers can send system details outside the enterprise boundary.

rules.title: Disable Windows Performance PerfTrack
rules.explanation: This setting controls Windows Diagnostics Infrastructure (WDI) PerfTrack scenario execution used for performance and responsiveness tracking.
rules.impact: PerfTrack can transmit diagnostic telemetry to Microsoft that is typically unnecessary in locked-down enterprise environments.

rules.title: Disable advertising ID
rules.explanation: This setting disables the Windows advertising identifier so that applications cannot use it for cross-app advertising interactions.
rules.impact: In enterprise environments, advertising identifiers are typically unnecessary and may expose usage or identity signals beyond organizational control.

rules.title: Enable Windows NTP client
rules.explanation: This setting enables the Windows Time NTP client so the system can synchronize time with configured time sources.
rules.impact: Accurate, synchronized system time underpins trustworthy security event timestamps and reliable incident investigation and correlation.

rules.title: Disable Windows NTP server
rules.explanation: This setting disables the Windows Time NTP server role so the system does not serve time to other clients.
rules.impact: Workstations and member servers should obtain time from authorized sources rather than acting as time servers, which can undermine trust in security event chronology.

rules.title: Restrict shared local app data between users
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows apps may share application data among users who installed the same app via the SharedLocal folder exposed through the Windows.Storage API.
rules.impact: Shared local app data can unintentionally expose confidential information from one user profile to another on the same system.

rules.title: Allow Microsoft accounts to be optional for Store apps
rules.explanation: This setting (MSAOptional) allows Windows Store and modern apps to be used with enterprise identities without requiring a Microsoft account.
rules.impact: Preferring centrally managed enterprise accounts for apps improves identity governance and reduces reliance on consumer Microsoft accounts for application data access.

rules.title: Hosted Windows Store apps blocked from WinRT API access
rules.explanation: This setting blocks Windows Store applications hosted from the Internet from accessing the Windows Runtime (WinRT) API directly (BlockHostedAppAccessWinRT).
rules.impact: Hosted apps with direct WinRT access increase the risk that untrusted content can invoke local platform APIs and execute unauthorized actions.

rules.title: Disable AutoPlay for non-volume devices
rules.explanation: This setting disables AutoPlay for non-volume devices such as cameras, phones, and similar MTP/media devices.
rules.impact: AutoPlay on connected mobile devices can automatically execute content; malware planted on a device may run when the device is attached.

rules.title: Disable AutoRun from autorun.inf
rules.explanation: This setting disables the AutoRun behavior that executes programs listed in an autorun.inf file on media.
rules.impact: Attackers can place a malicious executable name in autorun.inf so that connecting or inserting media starts malware automatically.

rules.title: Disable AutoPlay for all drives
rules.explanation: This setting disables AutoPlay across drive types so removable and other media do not automatically launch content.
rules.impact: Unrestricted AutoPlay increases the likelihood that malware on removable media starts without intentional user action.

rules.title: Windows Hello Face enhanced anti-spoofing enabled
rules.explanation: This setting enables enhanced anti-spoofing protections for Windows Hello Face authentication (EnhancedAntiSpoofing).
rules.impact: Without anti-spoofing, facial authentication may be deceived by presentation attacks, allowing unauthorized unlock or sign-in.

rules.title: Camera access prohibited
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether applications and the system may use camera devices on the computer.
rules.impact: Enabled cameras create privacy and data-exfiltration risks in high-security environments by allowing capture of sensitive visual information.

rules.title: Microsoft consumer experiences disabled
rules.explanation: This setting turns off Microsoft consumer experiences that surface tips, suggestions, and cloud-related recommendations in Windows.
rules.impact: Consumer experience features can generate unnecessary outbound communication and expose usage context that is typically restricted in enterprise deployments.

rules.title: PIN required for wireless display pairing
rules.explanation: This setting requires a PIN when pairing with Wireless Display (Miracast / Projecting) devices.
rules.impact: Pairing without a PIN increases the risk that unauthorized displays can connect and receive desktop content.

rules.title: Disable the password reveal button
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the password reveal button is available in credential entry dialogs.
rules.impact: Revealing typed passwords at sign-in increases the likelihood that credentials are observed by nearby attackers or camera-based shoulder surfing.

rules.title: Disable enumeration of administrator accounts during elevation
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether administrative accounts are enumerated and displayed when a user elevates privileges for an application (CredUI).
rules.impact: Enumerating privileged accounts during elevation can disclose high-value account names useful for targeted attacks.

rules.title: Diagnostic data (telemetry) level configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the amount of Windows diagnostic and usage data (telemetry) that may be sent to Microsoft.
rules.impact: Excessive diagnostic data sharing can disclose environment and usage details to a third party beyond what operational requirements justify.

rules.title: Feedback notifications disabled
rules.explanation: This setting prevents Windows from showing feedback notifications that prompt users to provide feedback to Microsoft.
rules.impact: Feedback prompts encourage users to submit environment and usage information to a third party, which is typically restricted in enterprise policy.

rules.title: Windows Insider preview builds disabled
rules.explanation: This setting restricts user access to Windows Insider / preview build controls so pre-release builds cannot be opted into on the system.
rules.impact: Preview builds are less stable and may introduce untested behavior that weakens security posture and complicates support.

rules.title: Delivery Optimization download mode configured
rules.explanation: This setting configures Delivery Optimization download mode (DODownloadMode), which controls how Windows Update content is obtained, including peer-to-peer sharing options.
rules.impact: Uncontrolled peer-to-peer update sharing can pull content from untrusted peers and expand the network attack surface beyond approved update sources.

rules.title: Application log overwrite retention configured
rules.explanation: This setting configures Application event log retention so events can be overwritten when the log reaches maximum size.
rules.impact: If the Application log does not overwrite when full, new events may be dropped and recent operational evidence becomes unavailable for investigation.

rules.title: Application log maximum size configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the maximum size of the Application event log.
rules.impact: An undersized Application log fills quickly and may lose recent events needed for troubleshooting and incident analysis.

rules.title: Security log overwrite retention configured
rules.explanation: This setting configures Security event log retention so events can be overwritten when the log reaches maximum size.
rules.impact: If the Security log does not overwrite when full, new security events may stop being recorded and investigative evidence is lost.

rules.title: Security log maximum size configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the maximum size of the Security event log.
rules.impact: An undersized Security log fills quickly and may fail to retain recent authentication and audit events required for incident investigation.

rules.title: Setup log overwrite retention configured
rules.explanation: This setting configures Setup event log retention so events can be overwritten when the log reaches maximum size.
rules.impact: If the Setup log does not overwrite when full, new setup-related events may be dropped and change history becomes incomplete.

rules.title: Setup log maximum size configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the maximum size of the Setup event log.
rules.impact: An undersized Setup log may lose recent installation and configuration events needed for audit and troubleshooting.

rules.title: System log overwrite retention configured
rules.explanation: This setting configures System event log retention so events can be overwritten when the log reaches maximum size.
rules.impact: If the System log does not overwrite when full, new system events may stop being recorded and operational evidence becomes unavailable.

rules.title: System log maximum size configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the maximum size of the System event log.
rules.impact: An undersized System log fills quickly and may lose recent system events needed for diagnosis and incident response.

rules.title: Data Execution Prevention for Explorer enabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Data Execution Prevention (DEP) is applied to Windows Explorer rather than being turned off for compatibility with legacy applications.
rules.impact: DEP helps prevent execution of code from non-executable memory regions and reduces the impact of certain memory-corruption malware techniques against Explorer.

rules.title: Heap termination on corruption for Explorer enabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows Explorer terminates the process when heap corruption is detected instead of continuing for legacy application compatibility.
rules.impact: Continuing to run after heap corruption can leave Explorer in an unstable state that malware or faulty code may further abuse.

rules.title: Shell protocol protected mode enabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the Windows shell protocol runs with protected-mode restrictions that limit folder access (PreXPSP2ShellProtocolBehavior).
rules.impact: Protected mode reduces the set of directories accessible through the shell protocol and narrows the attack surface for shell-based exploitation.

rules.title: HomeGroup joining prohibited
rules.explanation: This setting prevents the computer from joining a HomeGroup (DisableHomeGroup).
rules.impact: HomeGroup sharing can expose workstation data to other devices outside enterprise access controls, increasing the risk of unauthorized data disclosure.

rules.title: Location services disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables Windows location detection for Location and Sensors policies (DisableLocation).
rules.impact: Enabled location services can disclose workstation geographic information to applications and services and are typically unnecessary in enterprise environments.

rules.title: OneDrive file sync disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables OneDrive file storage and synchronization through the Next Generation Sync Client (NGSC).
rules.impact: Enabled OneDrive sync can result in unintentional storage of confidential files in cloud storage outside enterprise control.

rules.title: Remote Desktop password saving disabled
rules.explanation: This setting prevents Remote Desktop / Terminal Services clients from saving passwords on the local computer.
rules.impact: Saved remote-access passwords can be recovered by an attacker with local access and used to compromise additional systems reached from that host.

rules.title: Remote Desktop connections denied
rules.explanation: This setting denies inbound Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) connections through Terminal Services policy (fDenyTSConnections).
rules.impact: Allowing unrestricted RDP access increases remote attack surface and can enable credential theft, lateral movement, or malware delivery against workstations.

rules.title: Remote Desktop COM port redirection disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether COM ports can be redirected from the local client into a Remote Desktop session.
rules.impact: COM port redirection extends the remote session's device attack surface and can be used to introduce or exfiltrate data through serial devices.

rules.title: Remote Desktop drive redirection disabled
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether local drives can be redirected into a Remote Desktop session.
rules.impact: Drive redirection allows files to move freely between the remote session and local disks, which an attacker with session access can use to stage or remove malicious content.

rules.title: Disable LPT port redirection for Remote Desktop Services
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether LPT (parallel) ports on the client can be redirected into a Remote Desktop Services session. When disabled, local LPT ports are not available to the remote session.
rules.impact: LPT port redirection expands the session attack surface and can be abused to introduce or transfer unauthorized content between the client and the host. Restricting it reduces the risk of lateral data movement through redirected parallel ports.

rules.title: Disable Plug and Play device redirection for Remote Desktop Services
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Plug and Play devices on the client can be redirected into a Remote Desktop Services session. When disabled, PnP device redirection is blocked for RDP sessions.
rules.impact: Redirected Plug and Play devices can introduce untrusted hardware interfaces into the remote session and may be used to deliver malicious payloads. Disabling redirection limits this attack path.

rules.title: Require password prompt for Remote Desktop connections
rules.explanation: This setting requires users to enter credentials when establishing a Remote Desktop connection rather than using previously saved passwords automatically. It applies to Remote Desktop Services client authentication behavior.
rules.impact: Saved RDP credentials can be reused by anyone with access to the client workstation, enabling unauthorized access to remote systems under the stored account. Requiring a password prompt reduces reliance on cached credentials.

rules.title: Require secure RPC communication for Remote Desktop Services
rules.explanation: This setting requires Remote Desktop Services to use encrypted RPC connections for client-to-server communication. It strengthens the confidentiality and integrity of RDP control-channel traffic.
rules.impact: Without secure RPC, session setup traffic may be susceptible to interception or man-in-the-middle attacks. Enforcing encrypted RPC reduces exposure of Remote Desktop control communications.

rules.title: Set high encryption level for Remote Desktop connections
rules.explanation: This setting defines the minimum encryption level required for Remote Desktop Services client connections. A high encryption level requires strong encryption for session data.
rules.impact: Weak or insufficient encryption can allow intercepted RDP traffic to be decrypted or altered. A high minimum encryption level helps protect session confidentiality against network eavesdropping.

rules.title: Set time limit for active but idle Remote Desktop sessions
rules.explanation: This setting specifies how long an active Remote Desktop session may remain idle before it is disconnected. It limits unattended interactive RDP sessions on the server.
rules.impact: Idle sessions continue to consume server resources and may leave an authenticated desktop available for misuse. Time limits reduce resource exhaustion risk and shorten the window of unattended access.

rules.title: Set time limit for disconnected Remote Desktop sessions
rules.explanation: This setting specifies how long a disconnected Remote Desktop session may remain on the server before it is ended. Disconnected sessions continue to hold session state until this limit expires.
rules.impact: Long-lived disconnected sessions consume server resources and can accumulate until legitimate users are unable to connect. Ending them after a defined period reduces denial-of-service exposure and session sprawl.

rules.title: Delete temporary folders on Remote Desktop logoff
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether temporary folders created for a Remote Desktop session are deleted when the user logs off. Session-specific temporary data is removed at session end when enabled.
rules.impact: Temporary session folders may retain files or artifacts that contain sensitive information after logoff. Deleting them reduces residual data exposure on the Remote Desktop host.

rules.title: Prohibit downloading of RSS feed attachments
rules.explanation: This setting prevents download of enclosure attachments from RSS feeds through Internet Explorer feed handling. Feed properties that would otherwise allow enclosure download are restricted.
rules.impact: Feed enclosures can deliver untrusted files that contain malicious content. Blocking enclosure downloads reduces the risk of malware introduction through RSS attachments.

rules.title: Cortana disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables Cortana and related Windows Search assistant features (AllowCortana).
rules.impact: Cortana may retain search activity and related telemetry that can be sent to Microsoft, increasing the risk of organizational information disclosure.

rules.title: Cortana above lock screen disabled
rules.explanation: This setting prevents Cortana from being available while the device is locked (AllowCortanaAboveLock).
rules.impact: Cortana features on the lock screen can allow unauthenticated interaction and increase the risk of misuse by anyone with physical access to the workstation.

rules.title: Disable indexing of encrypted files
rules.explanation: This Windows Search policy controls whether encrypted files or stores may be indexed. When indexing of encrypted content is disallowed, Search does not process EFS-protected items for the index.
rules.impact: Indexing encrypted files can cause cryptographic protection to be removed for content that is ingested into the search index. Disabling this behavior helps keep sensitive encrypted data from being exposed through search artifacts.

rules.title: Search and Cortana location use prohibited
rules.explanation: This setting prevents Cortana and Windows Search from using device location information (AllowSearchToUseLocation).
rules.impact: Sharing workstation location with search services expands outbound disclosure of sensitive environment details beyond enterprise-approved data flows.

rules.title: Disable KMS client AVS online validation
rules.explanation: This setting disables automatic generation and transmission of Key Management Service (KMS) client activation validation data (AVS) to Microsoft. It applies to the Software Protection Platform on KMS-activated systems.
rules.impact: KMS client activation reporting can send environment-related licensing telemetry to Microsoft. Disabling AVS online validation limits outbound disclosure of activation-related information in enterprise environments.

rules.title: Microsoft Store apps disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables launching of Microsoft Store applications, including preinstalled and downloaded Store apps (DisableStoreApps).
rules.impact: Store apps can introduce unapproved software outside IT-controlled deployment processes and expand the workstation application attack surface.

rules.title: Microsoft Store automatic app updates enabled
rules.explanation: This setting configures automatic download and installation of updates for Microsoft Store applications (AutoDownload).
rules.impact: Missing application updates leave known vulnerabilities unpatched and increase the likelihood of successful exploitation against outdated Store apps.

rules.title: Microsoft Store OS upgrade offers disabled
rules.explanation: This setting prevents offering or initiating operating system upgrades through Microsoft Store (DisableOSUpgrade).
rules.impact: User-initiated OS upgrades outside controlled change processes can introduce compatibility issues and untested platform versions on managed workstations.

rules.title: Microsoft Store application removed
rules.explanation: This setting removes access to the Microsoft Store application on the workstation (RemoveWindowsStore).
rules.impact: An available Store client allows users to install software that has not been reviewed by IT and may contain vulnerabilities or unwanted components.

rules.title: Microsoft MAPS reporting disabled
rules.explanation: This setting opts the system out of Microsoft Active Protection Service (MAPS) cloud reporting for detected malware samples and related telemetry (SpynetReporting).
rules.impact: MAPS reports may include content sensitive to the organization and can disclose internal security-relevant information to an external service.

rules.title: Disable Windows Defender Watson generic report submission
rules.explanation: This setting disables submission of generic Windows Defender Watson debugger reports to Microsoft. Related diagnostic event data is retained locally rather than sent as Watson reports.
rules.impact: Watson diagnostic reports may contain organization-sensitive details from security events. Disabling submission limits outbound disclosure of that information.

rules.title: Windows Game DVR recording and broadcasting disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables Game DVR recording and broadcasting features on the workstation (AllowGameDVR).
rules.impact: Game recording and broadcasting can capture screen content that includes confidential information and is typically unnecessary in enterprise environments.

rules.title: Disable suggested apps in Windows Ink Workspace
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows Ink Workspace may present suggested or recommended applications. When disabled, app suggestion features in Ink Workspace are turned off.
rules.impact: Suggested-app features can collect usage and preference signals that may later be shared with Microsoft. Disabling suggestions reduces unnecessary telemetry related to user behavior.

rules.title: Prohibit user control over Windows Installer
rules.explanation: This Windows Installer policy determines whether standard users can change installation options that are normally reserved for administrators. When user control is disabled, non-administrators cannot override managed installer settings.
rules.impact: Allowing users to alter installer behavior can lead to unauthorized software installation or removal and weaken configuration control. Restricting installer control helps keep software changes under administrative governance.

rules.title: Prohibit always installing with elevated privileges
rules.explanation: This Windows Installer policy controls whether installations always run with system (elevated) privileges regardless of the user's rights. The AlwaysInstallElevated setting must not grant unrestricted elevated installer rights to standard users.
rules.impact: If AlwaysInstallElevated is enabled, a limited user can craft or run an MSI package that performs privileged actions such as creating local administrators or installing malware. Disabling elevated-always behavior closes a common privilege-escalation path.

rules.title: Require security prompt for Windows Installer scripts from Internet Explorer
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows Installer scripts invoked from Internet Explorer are treated as safe for scripting without user confirmation. When restricted, users are prompted before untrusted web-based installer scripts run.
rules.impact: Silent installation of untrusted scripted components can introduce malicious software without user awareness. Requiring a security prompt increases visibility and reduces unnoticed installer abuse from web content.

rules.title: Disable automatic restart sign-on
rules.explanation: This setting prevents Windows from automatically signing in the last interactive user after a system-initiated restart. Automatic restart sign-on and related credential reuse after reboot are restricted.
rules.impact: Automatic sign-on after restart can leave an unlocked or credential-backed session available without fresh authentication. Disabling it reduces unauthorized console access following system-managed reboots.

rules.title: Enable PowerShell script block logging
rules.explanation: This setting enables logging of PowerShell script blocks to the Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational event log. Executed script content is recorded for security monitoring and investigation.
rules.impact: PowerShell is a common post-exploitation and living-off-the-land tool. Script block logging provides forensic visibility into what code ran during an incident involving PowerShell.

rules.title: Disable PowerShell transcription
rules.explanation: This setting controls PowerShell transcription, which writes input and output from PowerShell sessions to plaintext transcript files. When transcription is disabled, session content is not recorded to those files.
rules.impact: Transcript files can capture passwords and other secrets entered or displayed during PowerShell use. Disabling transcription reduces the chance that sensitive values are left in cleartext on disk.

rules.title: Disable Basic authentication for the WinRM client
rules.explanation: This setting prevents the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client from using Basic authentication. Stronger authentication methods must be used for WinRM client connections when Basic is disabled.
rules.impact: Basic authentication transmits credentials in a reversible form that can be recovered from intercepted traffic. Disabling it on the WinRM client reduces credential exposure on the network.

rules.title: Disallow unencrypted traffic for the WinRM client
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the WinRM client may send unencrypted messages. When unencrypted traffic is disallowed, WinRM client communications must be protected in transit.
rules.impact: Unencrypted WinRM traffic can be intercepted or modified by an attacker on the network path. Requiring encryption protects the confidentiality and integrity of remote management sessions.

rules.title: Disable Digest authentication for the WinRM client
rules.explanation: This setting prevents the WinRM client from using Digest authentication. Digest is a weaker authentication mechanism compared with preferred WinRM authentication options.
rules.impact: Digest authentication provides limited protection and can expose authentication material to interception or offline attack. Disabling it reduces reliance on a weaker authentication method for remote management.

rules.title: Disable Basic authentication for the WinRM service
rules.explanation: This setting prevents the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) service from accepting Basic authentication. Incoming WinRM connections must use stronger authentication methods when Basic is disabled.
rules.impact: Accepting Basic authentication on the WinRM service exposes credentials to network interception. Disabling Basic authentication reduces cleartext credential risk for remote administration endpoints.

rules.title: Disable WinRM service automatic configuration
rules.explanation: This setting controls WinRM service automatic configuration that enables the service to listen for HTTP-based remote management requests on the default HTTP port. When disabled, WinRM does not auto-configure network listeners for remote administration.
rules.impact: An automatically configured WinRM listener expands the remote management attack surface and may facilitate credential-theft or remote abuse attempts. Disabling auto-configuration limits unintended remote exposure.

rules.title: Disallow unencrypted traffic for the WinRM service
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether the WinRM service may accept unencrypted messages. When unencrypted traffic is disallowed, managed hosts require encrypted WinRM service communications.
rules.impact: Unencrypted WinRM service traffic can be intercepted or altered by an attacker, enabling session compromise or further host attacks. Encryption protects remote management confidentiality and integrity.

rules.title: Prohibit WinRM service from storing RunAs credentials
rules.explanation: This setting prevents the WinRM service from storing RunAs credentials for plugins. Credential material associated with WinRM RunAs operations is not retained when this restriction is applied.
rules.impact: Stored RunAs credentials can be reused by an attacker who compromises the host to access other systems managed through WinRM. Preventing storage limits credential reuse after host compromise.

rules.title: Disable WinRM remote shell access
rules.explanation: This setting controls whether Windows Remote Shell (WinRS) access is permitted through WinRM. When disabled, remote shell sessions via WinRM are not allowed.
rules.impact: Remote shell access provides an interactive command channel that attackers frequently abuse for post-compromise activity. Disabling it reduces a powerful remote execution path on the host.

rules.title: Windows feature update deferral configured
rules.explanation: This setting enables deferral of Windows feature updates so administrators can control when feature update packages are installed (DeferFeatureUpdates).
rules.impact: Installing feature updates without staged testing can introduce application or driver incompatibilities and disrupt workstation availability.

rules.title: Configure Windows Update quality update deferral
rules.explanation: This Windows Update policy controls deferral of quality updates. It determines whether quality (security and reliability) updates may be delayed and how update timing is managed.
rules.impact: Deferred or inconsistently applied quality updates leave known vulnerabilities unpatched for longer periods. Proper quality-update configuration supports timely remediation of OS and application defects.

rules.title: Enable automatic updates
rules.explanation: This Automatic Updates policy controls whether Windows Update may automatically download and install updates. When automatic updates are enabled, systems receive updates without relying solely on manual installation.
rules.impact: Systems that do not receive updates regularly remain exposed to publicly known vulnerabilities. Automatic updating improves the likelihood that security fixes are applied consistently.

rules.title: Configure automatic update installation schedule
rules.explanation: This Automatic Updates setting defines the scheduled day for installing updates. It establishes a predictable maintenance window for applying Automatic Updates.
rules.impact: Without a defined installation schedule, update application may be delayed or inconsistently applied across systems. Scheduled installation supports timely patching while aligning with operational windows.

rules.title: Configure automatic restart after update installation
rules.explanation: This Automatic Updates setting controls whether Windows may automatically restart to complete update installation when users are logged on. It governs reboot behavior required to finish applying updates.
rules.impact: Updates that require a restart may remain only partially applied until the system reboots. Allowing necessary automatic restarts helps ensure security updates become fully effective.

rules.title: Enable screen saver
rules.explanation: This user policy enables the Windows screen saver for interactive sessions. When active, the configured screen saver can start after the idle timeout elapses.
rules.impact: An unlocked idle workstation can be used by anyone with physical access to view or act under the signed-in user's context. Enabling the screen saver is a prerequisite for idle session protection controls.

rules.title: Configure screen saver executable
rules.explanation: This user policy specifies the screen saver executable (SCRNSAVE.EXE) used when the screen saver is activated. It defines which screen saver binary Windows launches for the session.
rules.impact: An undefined or user-controlled screen saver configuration can leave idle-session protection incomplete or inconsistent. A managed screen saver executable supports enforceable workstation lock behavior.

rules.title: Require password on screen saver resume
rules.explanation: This user policy requires authentication when dismissing the screen saver. Resuming from the screen saver returns to a password-protected session rather than an unlocked desktop.
rules.impact: Without password protection, an activated screen saver does not prevent unauthorized interactive use of an idle session. Requiring credentials on resume protects confidential data on unattended workstations.

rules.title: Configure screen saver timeout
rules.explanation: This user policy sets the idle time, in seconds, before the screen saver activates. It defines how quickly an unattended interactive session enters screen saver protection.
rules.impact: A long or undefined idle timeout leaves the desktop unlocked for extended periods. A shorter managed timeout reduces the window for physical access abuse of an unattended session.

rules.title: Disable toast notifications on the lock screen
rules.explanation: This user policy prevents application toast notifications from appearing on the lock screen. Push notification content is not displayed while the device is locked.
rules.impact: Lock-screen notifications can reveal message previews or other sensitive details to anyone near the device. Disabling them reduces information disclosure from an unauthenticated console.

rules.title: Disable Microsoft Customer Experience Improvement Program implicit feedback
rules.explanation: This user policy disables implicit feedback participation in the Microsoft Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP) through Windows Assistance. Related usage feedback is not sent automatically.
rules.impact: CEIP feedback can include software usage details that organizations prefer to keep internal. Disabling implicit feedback limits outbound transmission of environment and usage information.

rules.title: Preserve zone information in file attachments
rules.explanation: This Attachment Manager setting preserves Internet zone (Mark of the Web) information on downloaded or received files. Zone metadata remains available so Windows can apply attachment security warnings and restrictions.
rules.impact: Removing zone information can cause downloaded malware to appear as a local trusted file and bypass attachment protections. Preserving zone data helps users and security features identify files from untrusted sources.

rules.title: Disable third-party suggestions in Windows Spotlight
rules.explanation: This Cloud Content policy prevents Windows Spotlight from showing suggestions from third-party providers. Spotlight content is limited when third-party suggestions are disabled.
rules.impact: Third-party Spotlight suggestions can involve sharing usage or interest signals outside the organization. Disabling them reduces disclosure of query and software-usage related information to external parties.

rules.title: Disable Windows Spotlight features
rules.explanation: This Cloud Content policy disables Windows Spotlight features for the user. Spotlight personalization and suggestion experiences governed by this setting are turned off.
rules.impact: Windows Spotlight features may disclose information about user interests, searches, or installed software to external services. Disabling Spotlight reduces that privacy and data-sharing exposure.

rules.title: Disable in-place file sharing
rules.explanation: This Explorer policy restricts in-place sharing of files from the user profile. Users cannot use the built-in sharing affordance controlled by NoInplaceSharing when the restriction is applied.
rules.impact: Convenient file sharing from the profile can expose confidential documents to unintended recipients or local attackers. Disabling in-place sharing reduces accidental and unauthorized data exposure.

rules.title: Always install with elevated privileges disabled for users
rules.explanation: This per-user policy controls whether Windows Installer always runs installations with elevated privileges for the signed-in user (AlwaysInstallElevated).
rules.impact: When AlwaysInstallElevated is enabled for users, a standard user can craft an MSI that performs privileged actions such as creating administrator accounts or installing malware.

rules.title: Prohibit Windows Media Player codec download
rules.explanation: This policy prevents Windows Media Player from automatically downloading codecs. Missing codecs are not retrieved from online sources when the restriction is enabled.
rules.impact: Automatically downloaded codecs can serve as a vehicle for delivering untrusted or malicious code to the workstation. Blocking codec download reduces that supply-chain and malware delivery risk.

rules.title: LLTDIO mapper I/O disabled on public networks
rules.explanation: This setting controls the Link-Layer Topology Discovery Mapper I/O (LLTDIO) driver on public networks used for network map discovery (AllowLLTDIOOnPublicNet).
rules.impact: Topology discovery on public networks can expose the host to unauthorized or attacker-controlled devices that participate in network mapping.

rules.title: LLTDIO mapper I/O driver disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables the Link-Layer Topology Discovery Mapper I/O (LLTDIO) driver used to discover and map the local network (EnableLLTDIO).
rules.impact: An enabled LLTDIO driver can interact with unauthorized devices during topology discovery and assist mapping of the internal network.

rules.title: LLTDIO mapper I/O prohibition on private networks configured
rules.explanation: This setting configures whether LLTDIO operation is prohibited on private networks as part of Link-Layer Topology Discovery Mapper I/O policy (ProhibitLLTDIOOnPrivateNet).
rules.impact: Misconfigured LLTDIO behavior on private networks can allow topology discovery interactions with unauthorized devices and increase network reconnaissance risk.

rules.title: LLTD Responder (RSPNDR) disabled on public networks
rules.explanation: This setting controls the Link-Layer Topology Discovery Responder (RSPNDR) driver on public networks (AllowRspndrOnPublicNet).
rules.impact: Responding to topology discovery on public networks can expose the host to unauthorized devices and assist network mapping by untrusted parties.

rules.title: LLTD Responder (RSPNDR) driver disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables the Link-Layer Topology Discovery Responder (RSPNDR) driver used to reply to network topology discovery requests (EnableRspndr).
rules.impact: An enabled responder can advertise the host during topology discovery and help unauthorized devices map the local network.

rules.title: LLTDIO mapper I/O prohibition on private networks configured
rules.explanation: This setting configures whether LLTDIO operation is prohibited on private networks as part of Link-Layer Topology Discovery Mapper I/O policy (ProhibitLLTDIOOnPrivateNet).
rules.impact: Misconfigured LLTDIO behavior on private networks can allow topology discovery interactions with unauthorized devices and increase network reconnaissance risk.

rules.title: Windows Connect Now UPnP registrar disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables the Windows Connect Now (WCN) UPnP registrar used for simplified wireless configuration transfer (DisableUPnPRegistrar).
rules.impact: WCN registrars simplify distribution of wireless configurations and can be abused to provision or obtain network settings during an attack.

rules.title: Windows Connect Now in-band 802.11 registrar disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables the Windows Connect Now (WCN) in-band IEEE 802.11 registrar used for wireless configuration provisioning (DisableInBand802DOT11Registrar).
rules.impact: An enabled 802.11 WCN registrar can transfer ready-made wireless configurations to other devices and create an abuse path for unauthorized network setup.

rules.title: Windows Connect Now Flash Config registrar disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables the Windows Connect Now (WCN) Flash Config registrar used for simplified wireless configuration transfer (DisableFlashConfigRegistrar).
rules.impact: Flash Config-based WCN provisioning can be misused to propagate wireless credentials or configurations to unauthorized devices.

rules.title: Windows Connect Now WPD registrar disabled
rules.explanation: This setting disables the Windows Connect Now (WCN) Windows Portable Device (WPD) registrar used for wireless configuration transfer (DisableWPDRegistrar).
rules.impact: WPD-based WCN registration can transfer wireless configurations to portable devices and increase the risk of unauthorized credential or profile disclosure.

rules.title: Enable device authentication using certificates (PKINIT)
rules.explanation: This setting allows devices to use public-key certificates for Kerberos device authentication (Device PKINIT).
rules.impact: Certificate-based device authentication strengthens machine identity assurance for Kerberos-protected connections compared with password-only machine accounts alone.

rules.title: Configure feature update deferral period
rules.explanation: This setting defines how long feature updates are deferred, controlling the pace at which new builds and features are received.
rules.impact: Receiving new features without staged testing can introduce incompatibilities and stability issues that affect availability and security posture.

rules.title: Windows quality update deferral period configured
rules.explanation: This setting defines the deferral period, in days, before quality updates are offered for installation (DeferQualityUpdatesPeriodInDays).
rules.impact: Without a controlled deferral and patching cadence, quality updates may be delayed inconsistently, leaving known OS and application vulnerabilities exposed longer than necessary.

rules.title: Disable legacy PC Health error reporting
rules.explanation: This setting disables automatic error report submission through the legacy PC Health Error Reporting component (DoReport).
rules.impact: Automatic error reports may include confidential diagnostic information that should remain within the organization.
